judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Card image 'Three people outdoors with Edinburgh Castle in the background.' linking to https://study.ed.ac.uk/ (the 'Study with us' card). The img is the only content of a focusable <a> (the accessible name comes from contents and equals the alt; there is no aria-hidden and no tabindex=-1, in the snapshot and on the live page). The alt describes the photo, not where the link goes. Understanding 1.1.1 puts linked images under Situation C (controls) with H30: 'When an image is the only content of a link, the text alternative for the image describes the unique function of the link'. The WAI functional-images tutorial says the same, and the Understanding examples use the destination ('Smallville Times', 'International Travel'). The heading link to the same URL right after it does not give the image link a name that describes its purpose: it only makes it a redundant link (H2 would merge the two, or the image link could be hidden from assistive technology). This is a real, if low-impact, 1.1.1 failure; 2.4.4 also applies.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The img is not in a link. It is the illustrative photo of the 'Research and teaching' card (a student taking a book from library shelves), directly above the h3 'Research and teaching' (the live page is the same). The alt names the topic the photo illustrates, and a library scene does depict research, so the alt does not describe something absent and does not mislead. At worst it repeats the heading: alt='' would be better for a decorative card photo, but redundant alt is best practice (axe's image-redundant-alt is a best-practice rule), not a 1.1.1 failure. The ACT rule 'Image accessible name is descriptive' accepts a name that describes the image's purpose. The check required a literal description of the scene, which is more than 1.1.1's equivalent-purpose test asks.
